title: Soft Washing & Pressure Washing in Chiefland, FL
description: Soft washing and pressure washing in Chiefland, FL to remove algae, mildew, and pollen from siding, roofs, decks, and drives. Done by our painting crews.
h1: Soft Washing and Pressure Washing in Chiefland, FL
heroIntro: In a damp, shaded town, algae and mildew are the most common exterior problem we see. We remove them with methods matched to each surface.

questions: How do I get green algae off my house?
Is soft washing safe for my roof?
How often should a house be washed in Florida?

sections.h2: Algae, mildew, and the Chiefland climate
body: Chiefland sits in a subtropical band where anything that stays damp long enough grows something. North walls, shaded eaves, the bottom of the siding, and roofs under trees are where green and black streaks show up first. Washing with water alone will not fix it, because the growth roots into the surface. Pressure washing in Chiefland, FL, done properly, means killing the organism and then rinsing it away.
Our article on mold and mildew on siding explains why the streaks come back when they are only blasted off.

Siding, stucco, painted trim, screens, and roofs get a soft wash: a cleaning solution applied at low pressure, given time to work, then rinsed. Concrete drives, sidewalks, and patios can take higher pressure. High pressure on wood or old paint can gouge the surface and push water behind siding, so we decide surface by surface.

sections.h2: Washing as the first step of a paint job
body: Every exterior paint job we take on begins with a wash. Mildew left alive under paint grows back through it, and paint over dirt or chalk will not bond. If you are planning exterior painting in Chiefland, the wash is part of the prep. If you only want the house cleaned, it can be booked on its own.
Spring pollen is another reason to wash. Our article on cleaning pollen stains covers that seasonal film.

sections.h2: How often to wash in Chiefland
body: Homes under heavy shade near the river or Manatee Springs often need a wash every year or two to keep algae from taking hold. Homes on open, sunny lots can usually go longer. A wash right after pollen season or before the summer storms is a cheap way to keep the paint looking fresh and to spot any early problems like cracked caulk or peeling trim.

We pre-wet and rinse plants, cover sensitive landscaping where needed, and work from the top down so runoff does not streak clean surfaces. See our main pressure washing service, or the Chiefland painters page for everything else we do locally.

faqs.q: Will soft washing damage my roof?
faqs.a: No. Roofs are cleaned with low pressure and a cleaning solution only, which treats the growth without blasting the surface.

faqs.q: How often should I wash my Chiefland home?
faqs.a: Shaded homes often benefit from a wash every year or two. Sunnier homes can usually go longer.

faqs.q: Can you wash my deck before staining it?
faqs.a: Yes. Washing and mildew treatment are always the first step of our deck and fence staining work.

faqs.q: Do you clean concrete driveways and patios too?
faqs.a: Yes. Concrete drives, walks, and patios can handle higher pressure than siding, and they can be added to a house wash or booked on their own.
